content: {"entries":[{"revises":[],"knowledge":[{"text":"Initial Skill's hold-and-invoke temperature-change guidance was followed when the candidate acquired the named target: it picked up the object and issued `heat`/`cool` with the appliance while still holding it, rather than moving it inside and toggling the door. Q9 (heat some egg) heated egg1 with microwave1 at Q9:7 and then placed it on countertop1 for success in 9 steps, while paired P9 moved the egg into the microwave and repeatedly opened/closed the door without heating, ending at the 50-step limit. Q3 and Q4 similarly cooled bread while holding it at fridge1 and then placed it, and Q4 and Q8 succeeded even though the fridge/microwave was closed at the moment of `cool`/`heat`, showing the verb does not require the appliance to be open. This supports the intended sequence but does not alone guarantee success; Q10 shows the same heat verb can be applied to a wrong object.","evidence":["diff","P9:14","P9:50","Q9:7","Q9:9","Q3:7","Q3:9","Q4:5","Q4:6","Q4:8","Q8:4","Q8:5","Q8:8","Q10:39"]},{"text":"Object selection was not reliably guided by the task noun. In Q10 (heat some mug and put it in coffeemachine), the candidate took cup1 from cabinet8 at Q10:25, heated the cup with microwave1 at Q10:39, and never acted on the required mug4, so it ended at the step limit; paired P10 did take mug4 at P10:42 but failed because it moved the mug into the microwave and toggled the door without heating. In Q7 (cool some pot), the candidate moved pan1 to stoveburner1 at Q7:8, a non-matching object, before taking pot2 only at Q7:49 and timing out. These cases show that applying the correct verb to an available but wrong object consumes actions and does not complete the named-object task.","evidence":["diff","P10:42","P10:45","P10:50","Q10:25","Q10:39","Q10:40","Q10:50","Q7:7","Q7:8","Q7:49","Q7:50"]},{"text":"The clean-then-place sequence was preserved in the current clean pair. Q1 (clean some spoon and put it in diningtable) opened drawer2, took spoon1, cleaned it with sinkbasin1 while holding it at Q1:8, and moved it to diningtable1 at Q1:10, succeeding in 10 steps; paired P1 used the same essential acquire-to-clean-to-place sequence and succeeded in 9 steps. The candidate's extra step was an initial countertop1 check, not a deviation from the clean/place clause.","evidence":["diff","P1:4","P1:5","P1:7","P1:9","Q1:1","Q1:5","Q1:6","Q1:8","Q1:10"]},{"text":"Searching under the new guidance was inconsistent: in some pairs the candidate found the target efficiently, but in hard or target-not-initially-visible cases it did not ensure coverage of unseen containers and still revisited known-empty locations. Q4 (cool bread) found bread1 on diningtable1 and succeeded in 8 steps versus P4's 47, and Q8 (hot apple) succeeded in 8 versus P8's 14, though those differences may reflect search-order or parent malformed actions. By contrast, Q6 (cool plate) repeatedly returned to cabinets1-3, countertops1-2, and drawers1-2 and never opened cabinet9, where paired P6 found plate1 and succeeded; Q6 ended at the 50-step limit. Q7 found pot2 only at Q7:49 and timed out while P7 had found, cooled, and placed pot2 earlier; Q10 never reached countertop3, where P10 found mug4 at P10:42, and instead acted on cup1. These are material parent-success/candidate-failure or both-fail cases showing search coverage remained incomplete under the joint edit.","evidence":["diff","P6:37","P6:38","P6:40","P6:43","Q6:8","Q6:10","Q6:17","Q6:25","Q6:42","Q6:50","P7:16","P7:18","P7:20","Q7:49","Q7:50","P10:42","P10:43","P10:50","Q10:25","Q10:39","Q10:50","Q4:3","Q4:4","Q4:8","P4:47","Q8:2","Q8:3","Q8:8","P8:14"]},{"text":"The action-format clause was associated with fewer malformed commands in several candidate runs but did not eliminate them. P2 emitted empty or reasoning-like actions at P2:1, P2:2, P2:6, P2:18, P2:29, and P2:32, while Q2 stayed on admissible commands through its 50-step run; P3 had an invalid action at P3:5 and P4 had invalid actions at P4:4, P4:28, and P4:32, while Q3 and Q4 completed without comparable malformed actions; P9 emitted invalid actions at P9:6, P9:21, and P9:45 while Q9 completed in 9 admissible steps. However Q6 still emitted inadmissible `go to cabinet 3` actions at Q6:6, Q6:23, Q6:29, Q6:35, Q6:40, and Q6:47, so the clause did not guarantee admissibility.","evidence":["diff","P2:1","P2:2","P2:6","P2:18","P2:29","P2:32","Q2:1","Q2:50","P3:5","Q3:9","P4:4","P4:28","P4:32","Q4:8","P9:6","P9:21","P9:45","Q9:9","Q6:6","Q6:23","Q6:29","Q6:35","Q6:40","Q6:47"]},{"text":"The initial Skill was a joint intervention, and current task-level results were mixed rather than uniformly improved. Candidate succeeded on Q1, Q3, Q4, Q8, and Q9 but failed on Q2, Q5, Q6, Q7, and Q10; parent succeeded on P1, P3, P4, P6, P7, and P8 and failed on P2, P5, P9, and P10. The clearest gain was Q9 over P9 on heat egg (hold-heat success versus microwave-door toggling failure), while Q6 and Q7 are clear regressions on cool plate and cool pot. Because several clauses changed together, the task-level mix should not be attributed to one clause; the direct clause-level evidence is in the hold-invoke successes, the Q10 wrong-object failure, and the Q6/Q7 search-coverage failures.","evidence":["diff","P1:9","Q1:10","P2:50","Q2:50","P3:10","Q3:9","P4:47","Q4:8","P5:50","Q5:50","P6:43","Q6:50","P7:20","Q7:50","P8:14","Q8:8","P9:50","Q9:9","P10:50","Q10:50"]}]}]}
